title: A Conformal Martingales Approach for Recurrent Concept Drift
venue: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 266: Conformal and Probabilistic Prediction with Applications
tldr: Pool ICM maintains a pool of past classifiers and reuses them upon recurrent drift detection, reducing retraining events by up to 94% while limiting accuracy loss to under 3 percentage points.
problem_and_motivation: In many real-world data streams, previously seen distributions reappear (recurrent concept drift), yet existing methods waste computational resources by retraining after every detected change instead of reusing previously trained models. A method that can recognize and exploit recurring patterns while maintaining statistical guarantees on drift detection is needed.
approach: Inductive Conformal Martingales (ICM) monitors data streams for exchangeability violations indicating concept drift.
A pool of previously trained classifiers is maintained and evaluated upon each detected drift event.
Each stored model is tested by merging its post-training nonconformity scores with recent data and checking exchangeability.
Models passing the exchangeability test are ranked by F1 score on recent data, with selection thresholded against historical performance.
A new model is trained and added to the pool only when no existing model satisfies both criteria.
Experiments on STAGGER, AIRLINES, and ELEC datasets benchmark against AWE and DWM state-of-the-art methods.
findings: num: Retraining events reduced by up to 94% on STAGGER dataset, training only 3-6 models versus ~100 detected drifts.
num: Relative gain in prediction instances ranges from 22% to 33% across datasets.
num: Accuracy on STAGGER with 10% noise reaches 0.933, compared to 0.948 for Standard ICM.
num: On AIRLINES, Pool ICM achieves 0.568 accuracy with 10 model retrainings versus 2.6 with Standard ICM.
num: On ELEC, model retrainings reduced to approximately one-third of detected changes.
num: Mean detection delay reduced from 215.09 to 18.39 on STAGGER when using cautious betting function.
num: False alarm rate reduced to 0.02 on STAGGER with cautious betting enabled.

topics.name: Anomaly Detection Algorithms for Personal Spending Data
topics.justification: Core contribution is an algorithm for detecting distribution changes (drift) in streaming data, directly relevant to anomaly detection in spending streams.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces Pool ICM, a novel framework that extends conformal martingale-based drift detection with model reuse for recurrent concept drift scenarios. The key innovation is combining statistical exchangeability testing with F1-score-based model selection from a pool of previously trained classifiers. This approach achieves significant computational savings by avoiding unnecessary retraining while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to always-retraining baselines. The work provides a principled, distribution-free method with provable guarantees on false detection rates, addressing a gap in existing reactive and heuristic drift handling approaches.
directly_justifies: num: Pool ICM reduces retraining events by up to 94% while maintaining accuracy within 3 percentage points of always-retraining.
The method uses distribution-free conformal martingales with provable false detection rate guarantees.
num: Relative gain in prediction instances ranges from 22% to 33% across benchmark datasets.
Model reuse is triggered by exchangeability testing combined with F1 score thresholding.
limits: Requires labeled data for both drift detection and model evaluation.
Accuracy slightly lower than always-retraining approaches on complex datasets.
Experiments limited to three benchmark datasets without financial domain validation.
Model pool growth management not fully addressed for very long streams.
topic_relevance.topic_relevance: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) received high relevance through subtopic 8.B, as the paper's core contribution is a drift detection algorithm for streaming data. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) received medium relevance through 6.B, since recurrent pattern detection is applicable to sequential spending data forecasting. Domains 1-5, 7, 9-14 were considered and rejected: the paper does not address Filipino demographics, financial behavior, expense categorization, budgeting, mobile design, privacy, engagement, evaluation frameworks, savings/debt management, or synthetic data generation. The paper's primary contribution is a general-purpose streaming classification algorithm rather than a personal finance system component.

limitations: Requires labeled data for both exchangeability testing and model selection.
Accuracy slightly lower than always-retraining baselines, particularly on complex real-world datasets.
Experiments limited to three benchmark datasets without financial domain validation.
Pool growth management and memory constraints for very long streams not fully addressed.
